{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693895518,"sessionID":"ses_e23eacbd3ffeJT7skaQA1qEsmg","part":{"id":"prt_1dc178c0f001I955OJiKDgtKtG","messageID":"msg_1dc1766da00132Lyqs6DBgWbu5","sessionID":"ses_e23eacbd3ffeJT7skaQA1qEsmg","type":"text","text":"The shift ended at minute 120 with all four customer-facing services at 0% errors and no throttles on. limits-svc was still at 24 replicas instead of its normal 8. Things were broken for a long stretch, though. partner-api (about 90% of revenue) failed until minute 49, and the three small storefronts were mostly down until minute 91, then down again from about minute 96 to 104.\n\n**What was wrong and what I did**\n\n1. **partner-api at about 4% errors (~$950/min).** The chain was partner-api → subscriptions-svc → sitemap-svc → audit-svc. audit-svc deploy v73 raised its minimum TLS version to 1.3, so sitemap-svc's calls to it failed the handshake. I rolled back v73 (minutes 41–46). While the rollback ran, the failed calls were retried and overloaded audit-svc, and partner-api errors jumped to about 58%. I turned on a 40% throttle on audit-svc for two minutes to stop the retries, and partner-api has been at 0% since minute 49.\n\n2. **ledger-svc (feeding limits-svc, which web-storefront and mobile-api use).** limits-svc had been overloaded by retries since about minute −14, before the page. Config cfg-43, applied at minute 45, then removed ledger-svc's `orders.write` permission scope, which made calls from limits-svc fail. I reverted the config at minute 62. Both services were still overloaded afterwards. Throttling didn't clear it: the first throttle on limits-svc was too small, and the two-minute throttle on ledger-svc didn't help either. Scaling them up did (limits-svc 8→24, ledger-svc 6→18) from minute 84.\n\n3. **cart-svc (used by admin-portal and mobile-api).** Deploy v93 leaked memory: memory at 99% and the service kept restarting. I rolled it back (minutes 63–68), which fixed the memory. It stayed overloaded until I scaled it 6→18 at minute 88.\n\n4. **Scale-down.** At minute 91 everything was clean, so I put all three back to their normal replica counts. limits-svc fell over again: its normal traffic has grown from about 650 to about 1,435 requests per second, which is more than 8 replicas can handle. I scaled it back to 24, and it recovered by minute 105. cart-svc and ledger-svc stayed healthy at their normal sizes.\n\n**Remaining costs and risks**\n- **Extra replicas:** 16 extra on limits-svc cost about $48/min from minute 104.\n- **Wasted mitigations:** I don't expect any $10,000 charges. Every rollback and config revert targeted a change the logs or diffs tied to a fault.\n- **For the next shift:** limits-svc should stay above 8 replicas, probably around 16 or more, as long as its traffic stays this high.\n- **feeds-svc:** CPU has been at about 0.98 since just before the page, with almost no errors. I didn't touch it, but it's at risk of overload.","time":{"start":1794693893135,"end":1794693895515}}}
